# Sloc Cloc and Code (scc)

![SCC illustration](./scc.jpg)

A tool similar to cloc, sloccount and tokei. For counting the lines of code, blank lines, comment lines, and physical lines of source code in many programming languages.

Goal is to be the fastest code counter possible, but also perform COCOMO calculation like sloccount, LOCOMO estimation for LLM-based development costs, estimate code complexity similar to cyclomatic complexity calculators and produce unique lines of code or DRYness metrics. In short one tool to rule them all.

Also it has a very short name which is easy to type `scc`.

If you don't like sloc cloc and code feel free to use the name `Succinct Code Counter`.

Licensed under MIT licence.

## Install

### Snap

A snap install exists.

`$ sudo snap install scc`

*NB* Snap installed applications cannot run outside of `/home` so you may encounter issues if you use snap and attempt to run outside this directory.

### Homebrew

Or if you have Homebrew installed

`$ brew install scc`

### Fedora

Fedora Linux users can use a COPR repository:

`$ sudo dnf copr enable lihaohong/scc && sudo dnf install scc`

### MacPorts

On macOS, you can also install via MacPorts

`$ sudo port install scc`

### Scoop

Or if you are using Scoop on Windows

`$ scoop install scc`

### Chocolatey

Or if you are using Chocolatey on Windows

`$ choco install scc`

### WinGet

Or if you are using WinGet on Windows

`winget install --id benboyter.scc --source winget`

### FreeBSD

On FreeBSD, scc is available as a package

`$ pkg install scc`

Or, if you prefer to build from source, you can use the ports tree

`$ cd /usr/ports/devel/scc && make install clean`

### Run in Docker

Go to the directory you want to run scc from.

Run the command below to run the latest release of scc on your current working directory:

```bash
docker run --rm -it -v "$PWD:/pwd"  ghcr.io/boyter/scc:master scc /pwd
```

### Manual

Binaries for Windows, GNU/Linux and macOS for both i386 and x86_64 machines are available from the releases page.

## Usage

Command line usage of `scc` is designed to be as simple as possible.
Full details can be found in `scc --help` or `scc -h`.

Note that you don't have to specify the directory you want to run against. Running `scc` will assume you want to run against the current directory.

You can also run against multiple files or directories `scc directory1 directory2 file1 file2` with the results aggregated in the output.

## Features

`scc` includes many features to help you count code accurately:

- Very fast and gets faster the more CPU you throw at it
- Accurate
- Works very well across multiple platforms without slowdown (Windows, Linux, macOS)
- Large language support
- Can ignore duplicate files
- Has complexity estimations
- You need to tell the difference between Coq and Verilog in the same directory
- cloc yaml output support so potentially a drop in replacement for some users
- Can identify or ignore minified files
- Able to identify many #! files
- Can ignore large files by lines or bytes
- Can calculate the ULOC or unique lines of code by file, language or project
- Supports multiple output formats for integration, CSV, SQL, JSON, HTML and more

## Complexity Estimates

Complexity estimates are provided for supported languages. The complexity estimate is an approximation similar to cyclomatic complexity. The intent is not to be perfect but provide a good enough indication of complexity.

Example output with complexity enabled:

```text
$ scc --complexity

Language                 Files     Lines   Blanks  Comments     Code Complexity
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Go                          13     7,340      896       455    5,989      1,076
```

## Unique Lines of Code (ULOC)

ULOC can be used to determine how many DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) code you have. It provides a measurement of unique lines of code.

To get ULOC output use the `--uloc` flag or `-u`:

```text
$ scc --uloc .
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Language                 Files     Lines   Blanks  Comments     Code Complexity    ULOC
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Go                          13     7,340      896       455    5,989      1,076   4,456
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

To calculate DRYness percentage use the `--dryness` flag or `-a`:

```text
$ scc --dryness .
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Language                 Files     Lines   Blanks  Comments     Code Complexity    DRYness
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Go                          13     7,340      896       455    5,989      1,076       74.4%
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

## COCOMO

COCOMO (Constructive Cost Model) calculates the estimated cost to build the code. scc uses the basic COCOMO model to provide estimates.

The COCOMO calculation is always run and will appear at the bottom of the output unless you use `--no-cocomo`.

Example:

```text
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Estimated Cost to Develop (organic) $12,517,562
Estimated Schedule Effort (organic) 35.93 months
Estimated People Required (organic) 30.95
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

You can customize COCOMO calculation with:

- `--avg-wage` - Set the average wage (default 56286)
- `--cocomo-project-type` - Change COCOMO model type: organic, semi-detached, embedded (default "organic")
- `--eaf` - Effort adjustment factor (default 1.0)
- `--currency-symbol` - Set currency symbol (default "$")

## LOCOMO

LOCOMO is an extension of COCOMO for calculating costs when using LLM (Large Language Model) based development approaches. It estimates token counts, API costs, and developer time when using AI assistants.

This is an experimental feature for estimating costs when using AI-powered development tools.

## Output Formats

scc supports multiple output formats for integration with other tools:

- `tabular` (default) - Human-readable table format
- `wide` - Wider table with additional statistics
- `json` - JSON format for programmatic processing
- `json2` - Alternative JSON format
- `csv` - CSV format
- `csv-stream` - Streaming CSV format
- `cloc-yaml` - YAML format compatible with cloc
- `html` - HTML report
- `html-table` - HTML table only
- `sql` - SQL CREATE and INSERT statements
- `sql-insert` - SQL INSERT statements only
- `openmetrics` - OpenMetrics/Prometheus format

Example:

```bash
scc --format json .
scc --format csv --output report.csv .
```

## Ignore Files

`scc` supports .ignore files inside directories that it scans. This is similar to how ripgrep, ag and tokei work. .ignore files are 100% the same as .gitignore files with the same syntax, and as such `scc` will ignore files and directories listed in them. You can add .ignore files to ignore things like vendored dependency checked in files.

By default scc will also respect .gitignore files.

## Large File Detection

scc can identify and optionally exclude large files from counting to focus on code that matters.

Use `--large-line-count` and `--large-byte-count` to set thresholds, and `--no-large` to exclude them from output.

## Minified/Generated File Detection

scc can identify minified and generated files and optionally exclude them from counts.

- `--min` - Identify minified files
- `--gen` - Identify generated files
- `--no-min` - Exclude minified files from output
- `--no-gen` - Exclude generated files from output
- `--no-min-gen` - Exclude both minified and generated files

## Remapping

You can remap file extensions to different languages using the `--count-as` flag:

```bash
scc --count-as jsp:htm,chead:"C Header" .
```

This maps `.jsp` files to HTML and `.chead` files to C Header.

You can also remap based on file content:

- `--remap-unknown` - Check unknown file types for a string and remap
- `--remap-all` - Check all files for a string and remap

Example:

```bash
scc --remap-unknown "-*- C++ -*-":"C Header" .
```

"""Development effort and token-budget estimates."""
import datetime
import math


def safe_div(a,b):
    if b:return a/b
    if not a:return math.nan
    return math.copysign(math.inf,a)


def fnum(x,places=2):
    if math.isnan(x):return 'NaN'
    if math.isinf(x):return '+Inf' if x>0 else '-Inf'
    return format(x,'.'+str(places)+'f')


def integer(x):
    if isinstance(x,float) and not math.isfinite(x):return '-9,223,372,036,854,775,808'
    return format(int(x),',')


def cocomo(code,opts):
    models={'organic':(2.4,1.05,2.5,.38),'semi-detached':(3.,1.12,2.5,.35),'embedded':(3.6,1.2,2.5,.32)}
    name=opts.cocomo_project_type
    coefficients=models.get(name)
    if coefficients is None and name.startswith('custom,'):
        parts=name.split(',')
        if len(parts)==5:
            try:coefficients=tuple(float(x) for x in parts[1:]);name='custom'
            except ValueError:pass
    if coefficients is None: name='organic';coefficients=models[name]
    a,b,c,d=coefficients
    try:effort=a*math.pow(code/1000,b)*opts.eaf
    except (ValueError,OverflowError):effort=math.nan
    try:schedule=c*math.pow(effort,d)
    except (ValueError,OverflowError):schedule=math.nan
    cost=effort*(opts.avg_wage/12)*opts.overhead
    people=effort/schedule if schedule else 0
    return dict(name=name,coefficients=coefficients,effort=effort,cost=cost,schedule=schedule,people=people)


def cocomo_text(code,opts,calc=None):
    calc=calc or cocomo(code,opts)
    name=calc['name'];a,b,c,d=calc['coefficients'];effort=calc['effort']
    currency=opts.currency_symbol
    if not opts.sloccount_format:
        return ['Estimated Cost to Develop ('+name+') '+currency+integer(calc['cost']),
                'Estimated Schedule Effort ('+name+') '+fnum(calc['schedule'])+' months',
                'Estimated People Required ('+name+') '+fnum(calc['people'])]
    rounded=math.floor(calc['cost']+.5) if math.isfinite(calc['cost']) else calc['cost']
    return [
        'Total Physical Source Lines of Code (SLOC)                     = '+integer(code),
        'Development Effort Estimate, Person-Years (Person-Months)      = '+fnum(effort/12)+' ('+fnum(effort)+')',
        ' (Basic COCOMO model, Person-Months = '+fnum(a)+'*(KSLOC**'+fnum(b)+')*'+fnum(opts.eaf)+')',
        'Schedule Estimate, Years (Months)                              = '+fnum(calc['schedule']/12)+' ('+fnum(calc['schedule'])+')',
        ' (Basic COCOMO model, Months = '+fnum(c)+'*(person-months**'+fnum(d)+'))',
        'Estimated Average Number of Developers (Effort/Schedule)       = '+fnum(calc['people']),
        'Total Estimated Cost to Develop                                = '+currency+integer(rounded),
        ' (average salary = '+currency+integer(opts.avg_wage)+'/year, overhead = '+fnum(opts.overhead)+')',
    ]


def locomo(code,complexity,opts):
    presets={'medium':(3.,15.,50.),'large':(10.,30.,30.),'small':(.5,2.,100.),'local':(0.,0.,15.)}
    name=opts.locomo_preset if opts.locomo_preset in presets else 'medium'
    inputprice,outputprice,tps=presets[name]
    if opts.locomo_input_price>0:inputprice=opts.locomo_input_price
    if opts.locomo_output_price>0:outputprice=opts.locomo_output_price
    if opts.locomo_tps>0:tps=opts.locomo_tps
    config=[10.,20.,5.,1.5,2.]
    parts=opts.locomo_config.split(',')
    if len(parts)==5:
        try:config=[float(x) for x in parts]
        except ValueError:pass
    output_per_line,input_per_line,weight,iterations,iteration_weight=config
    density=math.sqrt(complexity/code) if code else 0
    cycles=opts.locomo_cycles if opts.locomo_cycles>0 else iterations+iteration_weight*density
    multiplier=(1+weight*density)*cycles
    inputs=code*input_per_line*multiplier
    outputs=code*output_per_line*cycles
    cost=inputs/1e6*inputprice+outputs/1e6*outputprice
    return {
        'estimatedLLMCost':cost,'estimatedLLMInputTokens':inputs,
        'estimatedLLMOutputTokens':outputs,'estimatedLLMGenerationSeconds':outputs/tps,
        'estimatedLLMReviewHours':code*opts.locomo_review/60,'estimatedLLMPreset':name,
        'estimatedLLMAverageComplexityMultiplier':multiplier,'estimatedLLMCycles':cycles,
    }


def locomo_text(code,complexity,opts):
    d=locomo(code,complexity,opts)
    return [
        'LOCOMO LLM Cost Estimate ('+d['estimatedLLMPreset']+')',
        '  Tokens Required (in/out) '+fnum(d['estimatedLLMInputTokens']/1e6,1)+'M / '+fnum(d['estimatedLLMOutputTokens']/1e6,1)+'M',
        '  Cost to Generate '+opts.currency_symbol+integer(d['estimatedLLMCost']),
        '  Estimated Cycles '+fnum(d['estimatedLLMCycles'],1),
        '  Generation Time (serial) '+fnum(d['estimatedLLMGenerationSeconds']/60,1)+' minutes',
        '  Human Review Time '+fnum(d['estimatedLLMReviewHours'],1)+' hours',
        '  Disclaimer: rough ballpark for regenerating code using a LLM.',
        '  Does not account for context reuse, test generation, or heavy debugging.',
    ]


def size_text(size,opts):
    unit=opts.size_unit.lower()
    captions={
        'xkcd-kb':'1000 bytes during leap years, 1024 otherwise',
        'xkcd-kelly':'compromise between 1000 and 1024 bytes',
        'xkcd-imaginary':'used in quantum computing',
        'xkcd-intel':'calculated on pentium F.P.U.',
        'xkcd-drive':'shrinks by 4 bytes every year for marketing reasons',
        'xkcd-bakers':"9 bits to the byte since you're such a good customer",
    }
    divisors={'si':1000**2,'binary':1024**2,'mixed':1000*1024,
              'xkcd-kb':1024**4,'xkcd-kelly':1012**2,'xkcd-imaginary':1,
              'xkcd-intel':1023.937528**2,
              'xkcd-drive':(1000-4*(datetime.datetime.now().year-1990))**2,
              'xkcd-bakers':1152**2}
    if unit not in divisors:unit='si'
    text='¯\\_(ツ)_/¯' if unit=='xkcd-imaginary' else fnum(size/divisors[unit],3)
    lines=[captions[unit]] if unit in captions else []
    lines.append('Processed '+str(size)+' bytes, '+text+' megabytes ('+unit.upper()+')')
    return lines

    presets={'medium':(3.,15.,50.),'large':(10.,30.,30.),'small':(.5,2.,100.),'local':(0.,0.,15.)}
    name=opts.locomo_preset if opts.locomo_preset in presets else 'medium'
    inputprice,outputprice,tps=presets[name]
    if opts.locomo_input_price>0:inputprice=opts.locomo_input_price
    if opts.locomo_output_price>0:outputprice=opts.locomo_output_price
    if opts.locomo_tps>0:tps=opts.locomo_tps
    config=[10.,20.,5.,1.5,2.]
    parts=opts.locomo_config.split(',')
    if len(parts)==5:
        try:config=[float(x) for x in parts]
        except ValueError:pass
    output_per_line,input_per_line,weight,iterations,iteration_weight=config
    density=math.sqrt(complexity/code) if code else 0
    cycles=opts.locomo_cycles if opts.locomo_cycles>0 else iterations+iteration_weight*density
    multiplier=(1+weight*density)*cycles
    inputs=code*input_per_line*multiplier
    outputs=code*output_per_line*cycles
    cost=inputs/1e6*inputprice+outputs/1e6*outputprice
    return {
        'estimatedLLMCost':cost,'estimatedLLMInputTokens':inputs,
        'estimatedLLMOutputTokens':outputs,'estimatedLLMGenerationSeconds':outputs/tps,
        'estimatedLLMReviewHours':code*opts.locomo_review/60,'estimatedLLMPreset':name,
        'estimatedLLMAverageComplexityMultiplier':multiplier,'estimatedLLMCycles':cycles,
    }


def locomo_text(code,complexity,opts):
    d=locomo(code,complexity,opts)
    return [
        'LOCOMO LLM Cost Estimate ('+d['estimatedLLMPreset']+')',
        '  Tokens Required (in/out) '+fnum(d['estimatedLLMInputTokens']/1e6,1)+'M / '+fnum(d['estimatedLLMOutputTokens']/1e6,1)+'M',
        '  Cost to Generate '+opts.currency_symbol+integer(d['estimatedLLMCost']),
        '  Estimated Cycles '+fnum(d['estimatedLLMCycles'],1),
        '  Generation Time (serial) '+fnum(d['estimatedLLMGenerationSeconds']/60,1)+' minutes',
        '  Human Review Time '+fnum(d['estimatedLLMReviewHours'],1)+' hours',
        '  Disclaimer: rough ballpark for regenerating code using a LLM.',
        '  Does not account for context reuse, test generation, or heavy debugging.',
    ]


def size_text(size,opts):
    unit=opts.size_unit.lower()
    captions={
        'xkcd-kb':'1000 bytes during leap years, 1024 otherwise',
        'xkcd-kelly':'compromise between 1000 and 1024 bytes',
        'xkcd-imaginary':'used in quantum computing',
        'xkcd-intel':'calculated on pentium F.P.U.',
        'xkcd-drive':'shrinks by 4 bytes every year for marketing reasons',
        'xkcd-bakers':"9 bits to the byte since you're such a good customer",
    }
    divisors={'si':1000**2,'binary':1024**2,'mixed':1000*1024,
              'xkcd-kb':1024**4,'xkcd-kelly':1012**2,'xkcd-imaginary':1,
              'xkcd-intel':1023.937528**2,
              'xkcd-drive':(1000-4*(datetime.datetime.now().year-1990))**2,
              'xkcd-bakers':1152**2}
    if unit not in divisors:unit='si'
    text='¯\\_(ツ)_/¯' if unit=='xkcd-imaginary' else fnum(size/divisors[unit],3)
    lines=[captions[unit]] if unit in captions else []
    lines.append('Processed '+str(size)+' bytes, '+text+' megabytes ('+unit.upper()+')')
    return lines

"""Portable regression tests for the independently implemented CLI."""
import csv
import io
import json
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import tempfile
import unittest

EXE = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / 'executable')


class CounterTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.root = Path(self.temp.name)

    def tearDown(self):
        self.temp.cleanup()

    def write(self, name, text):
        path = self.root / name
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        path.write_bytes(text.encode() if isinstance(text, str) else text)
        return path

    def run_cli(self, *args):
        return subprocess.run([EXE, *map(str, args)], capture_output=True, text=True, check=False)

    def report(self, *flags, path=None):
        result = self.run_cli('-f', 'json', *flags, path or self.root)
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        return json.loads(result.stdout)

    def test_language_metrics(self):
        self.write('main.py', '# doc\n\n"""docstring\ntext\n"""\nif value:\n    print(value)\n')
        self.write('main.js', '// note\nconst x = 1;\n\nif (x && y) {\n}\n')
        rows = {row['Name']: row for row in self.report('--by-file')}
        self.assertEqual([rows['Python'][k] for k in ['Lines','Code','Comment','Blank','Complexity']], [7,2,4,1,1])
        self.assertEqual([rows['JavaScript'][k] for k in ['Lines','Code','Comment','Blank','Complexity']], [5,3,1,1,2])
        self.assertEqual(rows['Python']['Files'][0]['Filename'], 'main.py')

    def test_empty_file_and_uloc(self):
        path = self.write('empty.c', '')
        row = self.report('--by-file', '-u', path=path)[0]
        self.assertEqual(row['Lines'], 0)
        self.assertEqual(row['Count'], 1)
        self.assertEqual(row['ULOC'], 1)
        self.assertEqual(row['Files'][0]['Uloc'], 0)
        self.write('empty.c', 'x\n x\nx\n\n')
        row = self.report('-u')[0]
        self.assertEqual(row['ULOC'], 2)
        self.assertEqual(row['Lines'], 4)

    def test_nested_comments_and_raw_strings(self):
        self.write('main.rs', '/* first\n/* nested */\n\n*/\nx\n')
        self.write('main.go', 'var s = `a\\`\n// comment\n\n')
        rows = {r['Name']:r for r in self.report()}
        self.assertEqual([rows['Rust'][k] for k in ['Code','Comment','Blank']], [1,4,0])
        self.assertEqual([rows['Go'][k] for k in ['Code','Comment','Blank']], [1,1,1])

    def test_ignore_files(self):
        self.write('.gitignore', 'ignored.py\nvendor/\n')
        self.write('main.py', 'x\n')
        self.write('ignored.py', 'x\n')
        self.write('vendor/helper.py', 'x\n')
        self.assertEqual(self.report()[0]['Count'], 1)
        self.assertEqual(self.report('--no-gitignore')[0]['Count'], 3)
        rows = {r['Name']:r for r in self.report('--count-ignore')}
        self.assertIn('gitignore', rows)

    def test_filters_and_detection(self):
        self.write('a.py', 'x\n')
        self.write('b.js', 'x\n')
        self.write('script', '#!/usr/bin/env python3\nx\n')
        self.write('unknown.extension', '#!/usr/bin/env python3\nx\n')
        rows = self.report('-i', 'py')
        self.assertEqual([(r['Name'],r['Count']) for r in rows], [('Python',1)])
        self.assertEqual(self.report('-i', '.py'), [])
        self.assertEqual(self.report('--no-large','--large-line-count','1'), [])
        rows = {r['Name']:r for r in self.report('--count-as','js:Python')}
        self.assertEqual(rows['Python']['Count'], 3)

    def test_minified_and_generated(self):
        self.write('large.js', 'x'*255)
        self.write('generated.js', '// Code generated. DO NOT EDIT.\nx\n')
        rows = {r['Name']:r for r in self.report('--min-gen')}
        self.assertIn('JavaScript (min)', rows)
        self.assertIn('JavaScript (gen)', rows)
        self.assertEqual(self.report('--no-min-gen'), [])

    def test_duplicates_and_path_identity(self):
        p = self.write('main.py', 'abc\n')
        self.write('copy.py', 'abc\n')
        row = self.report('-d','--by-file')[0]
        self.assertEqual(row['Count'], 1)
        self.assertEqual(row['Files'][0]['Hash'], {})
        result = self.run_cli('-f','json',p,p)
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(result.stdout)[0]['Count'], 1)

    def test_binary_detection(self):
        self.write('binary.py', b'ab\0c\n')
        self.write('comment.py', b'# ab\0c\n')
        self.assertEqual(self.report()[0]['Count'], 1)
        self.assertEqual(self.report('--binary')[0]['Count'], 2)

    def test_formats_and_output(self):
        self.write('a.py', 'x\n')
        text = self.run_cli('--ci','--no-cocomo','--no-size',self.root).stdout
        self.assertTrue(text.startswith('-'*79+'\nLanguage'))
        report = self.run_cli('-f','csv',self.root).stdout
        rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(report)))
        self.assertEqual(rows[1], ['Python','1','1','0','0','0','2','1','0'])
        dest = self.root / 'result.csv'
        r = self.run_cli('-f','csv','-o',dest,self.root)
        self.assertEqual(r.stdout, f'results written to {dest}\n')
        self.assertTrue(dest.read_text().startswith('Language,Lines,Code'))

    def test_json2_costs(self):
        self.write('a.txt', 'x\n'*1000)
        r = self.run_cli('-f','json2','--locomo',self.root)
        d = json.loads(r.stdout)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(d['estimatedCost'], 27014.4)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(d['estimatedLLMInputTokens'], 30000)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(d['estimatedLLMOutputTokens'], 15000)

    def test_meta_cli(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.run_cli('--version').stdout, 'scc version 3.7.0\n')
        self.assertIn('Python (py,pyw,pyi)\n', self.run_cli('--languages').stdout)
        r = self.run_cli('--bogus')
        self.assertEqual(r.returncode, 1)
        self.assertTrue(r.stderr.startswith('Error: unknown flag: --bogus\nUsage:'))
        r = self.run_cli(self.root/'missing')
        self.assertEqual(r.returncode, 1)
        self.assertTrue(r.stdout.startswith('file or directory could not be read: '))

    def test_mcp(self):
        request = {'jsonrpc':'2.0','id':1,'method':'initialize','params':{'protocolVersion':'2024-11-05','capabilities':{},'clientInfo':{'name':'test','version':'1'}}}
        r = subprocess.run([EXE,'--mcp'], input=json.dumps(request)+'\n', capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
        response = json.loads(r.stdout)
        self.assertEqual(response['result']['serverInfo'], {'name':'scc','version':'3.7.0'})


if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()

Run `./compile.sh`. It creates `./executable`, a self-contained Python archive

Run the portable regression tests with:

- `src/language_rules.json`: vocabulary established by independent CLI probes.

- `src/formats.py`: tabular, JSON, CSV, HTML, SQL, YAML, and metrics output.
- `src/mcp.py`: JSON-RPC stdio interface.

manual, without using an existing implementation. Development-only scripts in
`tools/` make and compare small experimental inputs. They are not part of the
executable and are not needed to build it. Build outputs, captured observations,
and the locally retained reference executable are ignored by Git.

Run `./compile.sh`. It creates `./executable`, a self-contained Python archive
